sections.overview: Pterapherapteryx sexalata is a geometrid moth ranging across much of Europe and eastwards into Siberia.
sections.identification: It is a small moth with a wingspan of about twenty-two to twenty-six millimetres.
sections.habitat: It favours damp places where willows grow, including woodland, hedgerows, fens, wetlands and riverbanks.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on willows (Salix); British records call sallow the larval foodplant.
sections.behavior: In southern England there are usually two broods; elsewhere in Britain, a single brood is more usual.
sections.reproduction: The pupa overwinters, and the caterpillars feed in autumn on their willow hosts.
sections.ecology: The moth is associated with wet, willow-rich habitats; records from Britain show that local flight periods vary within the country.
sections.conservation: No global conservation assessment was found in the sources consulted.
